texts: The atrial reversal wave of pulmonary vein flow (PVa) is related to left atrial contraction: B.

Pulmonary venous flow has a forward systolic wave (S), a forward diastolic wave (D) and a small reversal at the end of diastole (PVa), when the contracting atrium pushes some blood back into the veins.
With high filling pressures the systolic wave becomes smaller than the diastolic one, and the PVa wave becomes larger and longer.
A PVa that lasts longer than the mitral A wave, by more than about 30 ms, indicates a high left ventricular end-diastolic pressure; the reverse is normal.
In the picture, two waves rush down the money pipes, and only when Robin's arms squeeze the red lobby does a small splash leap back up.
Memory hook: the lobby's squeeze sends the splash back up the pipes.
